## What the reviewer flagged

- Nothing. EditScenarioClient.tsx now always includes the draft/default roles (derived from legacy userRole/aiRole when no Role rows exist) in the Save payload, so Add Issue is enabled without hidden setup and the PATCH route's `initializing` branch atomically creates the two draft Role rows plus the Issue in one transaction, gated behind an explicit authorized Save (page.tsx only reads via GET, no writes). The route re-locks the scenario row with `FOR UPDATE` and re-reads before initializing, preventing duplicate Role rows on concurrent/retried saves. Persona links/copy are left untouched unless the author edits them, and roleType is only kept in sync when a Role is renamed — no ambiguous auto-assignment. Multi-side validation (>2 roles rejects Issues), ownership checks (404 for strangers, 401 for anonymous, ownership check in /api/personas/[id]/route.ts unmodified), and direction/number validation in parseIssuesInput are all intact and unmodified. The new integration test file exercises legacy save, edit-and-resave, concurrent first saves, unauthorized/anonymous access, invalid input, transactional rollback on a failed Scenario write, and the >2-sides rejection, all against real PostgreSQL. Reviewed code matches both locked unit test (EditScenarioClient.test.tsx) and locked Playwright acceptance spec (slice-13-legacy.spec.ts) expectations exactly (testids, payload shapes, persisted values across reloads). No locked test files were touched; only the allowed paths were changed.
